title: Verify Linux debug command channel parity
changes: Record a same-seed inspection and neutral-step comparison across menu, local-control CLI and interactive command console.
validation: Three isolated interpreter sessions used the same protected public synthetic ROM, seed and existing Linux runtime. The full 16-byte read-only inspection matched across channels without guest mutation; origin and one-frame endpoint state hashes, frame, clock, registers, CPSR, keys, PC, mode, pause and remaining budget matched. Each GUI closed normally and protected inputs stayed unchanged (dbg27-linux-threeway-guarded3-zwhascbo). Console screenshots were reviewed.

The navigation-only unit passed and located the default inspect form (dbg27-linux-inspect-route-5042xmbn). Earlier comparison drivers stopped before parity: rapid simulated keys collapsed, a return retained the selected row, or a section click did not land (723el4jv, ai_smwm_, q3fqberg); the guarded final run passed. A separate physical pad was detected but its input window timed out without an observed button (dbg27-linux-physical-pad-x3e2zrpt).
limitations: The selected synthetic interpreter scenario does not establish general Linux integration, real controller input, native Windows, other commands or a source-to-executable rebuild match. The tested executable SHA-256 is 2f53ae682ea1643d92a0136261aba2c5b396a36dac014648d4d8e6f7277eb50f.
